sentences.text: Hamadasuchus is characterized by lateromedially compressed and serrated teeth within a deep snout.
Its slightly heterodont dentition features three distinct tooth morphologies in the lower jaw.
Fossils of Hamadasuchus have been found in the Kem Kem Formation in southeastern Morocco.
The genus Hamadasuchus was described by Buffetaut in 1994.
Hamadasuchus was originally classified in the family Trematochampsidae but now belongs to the family Peirosauridae.
The type species of Hamadasuchus is H. rebouli, while H. taouzensis is a proposed species described by Nicholl et al. in 2021.
Nicholl et al. in 2021 suggested that Antaeusuchus might be a synonym of Hamadasuchus.
Hamadasuchus lived during the Albian and Cenomanian stages of the Late Cretaceous, between 106.3 and 93.9 million years ago.
